analysis.title: Market Internal Insight: Strongest Bullish Setup YTD, Expect SPX 10%+ Higher in 3 Months
key_insights: UBS US Equity Derivatives desk says systematic positioning is washed out. Risk Control exposure is 55%, the lowest since the April 2025 tariff selloff. CTA equity exposure is -5%.

The desk expects SPX to rise at least 10% over the next three months in a lower-volatility grind higher. Its reasons are limited remaining systematic selling, resilient real-money demand, short squeeze risk and possible CTA and Risk Control re-buying.

The desk had expected a Monday low. It was wrong on that point because buying overwhelmed the one remaining systematic seller, Risk Control. It says very little systematic selling should remain after today.
Prior Risk Control washouts were followed by SPX gains: 55% on Aug 6, 2024 was followed by +17% over 4 months, and 30% on Apr 10, 2025 was followed by +24% over 4 months.
Negative CTA exposure has historically been a bottoming signal, particularly when real-money investors are not selling. The desk says the downside feedback loop has largely been removed.

Real-money support comes from retail, foreign investors and corporate buybacks, which return next week. The desk expects news-driven selloffs to be shallow, though discretionary investors can still sell on negative headlines.

Intraday excess flow as of 1:00pm was +$34bn buying in the S&P 500 with SPY +2.4%, and +$60bn buying in Nasdaq with QQQ +3.2%. Nasdaq buying is led by single stocks, likely retail demand and short covering.
Leverage ETFs are estimated to buy +$24bn, of which $20bn is in QQQ and tech ($10bn semis, $8bn QQQ, $2bn other tech). Top dollar buys are NVDA, AMD, MU, AVGO, AAPL, MSFT, INTC, TSLA, TXN and AMZN.
The UBS short basket (UBXXSHRT) was +4.10% at the time of writing, which the desk reads as a short squeeze.

CTAs have barely bought so far today. Five buy triggers for ES1 sit between 7654.6 (+1.2%) and 7715.9 (+2.0%), and five for RTY1 sit between 2849.7 (+0.5%) and 2925.9 (+3.1%). NQ1 has no close buy triggers.

Multi-strat funds may have cut risk during Asia hours as realized volatility pushed some pods toward risk limits. Risk Control is estimated to sell only about $5bn at SPX +2.4%, against $85-115bn of selling estimated earlier today.
UBS PB long/short ratio is 1.91x, the 2nd percentile vs 1 year.
risk_factors: Negative headlines can still trigger knee-jerk selling from discretionary investors.
Multi-strat funds could cut more risk if realized volatility stays high.
Risk Control is still estimated to sell $85-115bn today, although the desk estimates about $5bn at current SPX levels.
vol_and_positioning: Risk Control exposure is 55%, 1st percentile vs 1Y and 22nd percentile vs 5Y, the lowest since the tariff selloff.
CTA global equity exposure is -5%, 5th percentile vs 1Y and 23rd percentile vs 5Y.
UBS PB long/short ratio is 1.91x, 2nd percentile vs 1Y.
Realized volatility spiked, pushing some multi-strat pods toward risk limits. The desk expects a lower-volatility rally from here.
Short squeeze risk: UBS short basket +4.10% intraday.
Nasdaq cash volume was 142% of average, S&P 500 cash volume slightly below average, and NQ1 and ES1 futures volume 125% and 119% of average.
